title: Per-model calibration observability, default quant profile signatures, and fallback heuristics for catalog
creator: Anika Patel
description:
Goal: Establish per-model default quantization recommendations in the catalog that are accompanied by machine-readable calibration signatures, a continuous observability surface, and deterministic fallback heuristics when accuracy regressions are detected. This ticket delivers: 1) a calibration observability schema and dashboard metrics, 2) an offline+online calibration workflow for producing and validating per-model default profiles (FP8/INT8/FP16 mixes), 3) a compact 'calibration signature' artifact stored with the model card used for CI gating and runtime compatibility checks, and 4) a rollout/fallback plan (shadowing, canary, automatic rollback) for deploying quant defaults to Hosted/Dedicated/Private runtimes. Rationale: prior ad hoc quant defaults have led to regressions on edge-case tasks and unpredictable rollouts for Dedicated/Private customers. We need a reproducible artifact that certifies a quant profile for a given model version and input distribution, plus runtime guardrails to preserve SLOs and quality. Key deliverables: - Calibration harness: two-pass approach (offline full-eval over curated reference suites + online adaptive calibration using live/representative samples) with tooling to produce per-model candidate profiles and aggregate accuracy deltas vs float32 baseline. - Calibration signature: small JSON blob (deterministic checksum, reference dataset fingerprint, KL/JS/Accuracy metrics, token-level error distribution summary, recommended fallback chain) that is stored in model metadata and used by CI and runtime. - Observability: per-model calibration_score time-series, regression_alerts, distribution_drift metric, canary_traffic_status, and a console widget that surfaces per-route quality impact of applied quant. - Runtime guardrails: configurable thresholds that trigger automatic fallback (e.g., if calibration_score drops below threshold OR KL divergence > 0.02 for sensitive tasks -> fall back to safer quant or FP16), with configurable policy per customer tier (hosted=auto, dedicated=warn+auto, private=warn-only by default). - CI gating: signature verification and shadow run acceptance criteria before allowing model catalog default to be used by production routes. - Rollout plan: shadow for 100% offline, canary to 1% traffic for 24h with active quality probes, escalation to 10%/50%/100% or rollback on alert. Acceptance criteria: - For each model in the catalog, produce at least one recommended default profile (one-liner: e.g. fp8-dq-s14 for chat, int8-q4a for embeddings) with an attached calibration_signature. - Demonstrate calibration harness on 3 diverse open models and show numeric deltas <= target thresholds for held-out evaluation tasks. - Console shows per-model calibration_score and emits a regression_alert if metrics cross thresholds during canary. - CI prevents catalog promotion if signature missing or shadow runs exceed allowed delta. Dependencies: calibration corpora, eval harness (REPO: evals), console instrumentation, runtime fallback APIs. Security review: required for any storage of customer-sensitive sample inputs. Release target: model-catalog-2025.03. Notes on scope: this ticket focuses on orchestration, schema, and observability; low-level kernel/quant algorithm changes handled in ENG-kernel teams.

Edge cases and trade-offs: - Strict thresholds reduce rollout velocity but increase safety; propose a per-model risk tier to relax thresholds for low-risk models. - Online adaptive calibration can drift and overfit: use holdout evaluation and rolling windows; log calibration changes for audit. - Private customers may want to opt out of automatic fallback; we will provide an explicit flag in model-card metadata and extend RBAC controls.
comments: 2025-01-12 — Kickoff: synced with PM (Rosa Kim) and Console eng. Action items: finalize calibration signature schema, identify initial 3 models for pilot (mosaic-7b, redwood-alpha-3b, open-llama-13b).

2025-01-20 — Prototype: offline harness produced candidate FP8/INT8 profiles for mosaic-7b. Observed BLEU-like metric drop of 0.9% for FP8 quant vs float32 on summarization eval; KL divergence 0.015. Marked as candidate 'fp8-s14' with calibration signature drafted.

2025-01-28 — Design review: Product requested explicit user-visible note in model card when default quant differs from runtime applied quant (e.g., user-enforced FP16). Agreed to add 'applied_quant' field in telemetry.

2025-02-05 — Security note: private deployment owners asked for opt-out and audit log for any calibration artifact uploaded to their VPC. Design: calibration_signature stored in customer-controlled metadata bucket for Private deployments. Need security review.
2025-02-14 — Implementation: added calibration_score timeseries to model metrics API (proposal PR #5892). Console team to add widget. Planning shadow canary for redwood-alpha-3b next week.
2025-02-19 — QA: wrote canary acceptance script that fails if top-1 token distribution KL > 0.02 or task accuracy delta > 1.5% on sensitive probes. Running 24h shadow now.
